title: AI Engineer - Agent Platform
description:
**AI Engineer \\- Agent Platform** 





 Mangaluru, Karnataka \\| Onsite, 5 days a week \\| Full\\-time
 




  





**About the role** 




 This position designs and owns the agent layer of a multi\\-product consumer platform: multi\\-agent systems in Python, exposed as REST and streaming APIs and consumed by the wider platform. The architecture is deliberately provider\\- and framework\\-agnostic; the model and orchestration library behind a feature are treated as configuration decisions rather than architectural ones, and both are expected to change as the market moves. The role therefore centres less on any one vendor’s SDK and more on the durable engineering underneath: agent topologies, tool and interop protocols, context and caching strategy, model routing, token economics, and the observability to know what any of it is costing.
 



 This is a senior, hands\\-on seat demanding real coding strength. Agent frameworks make the first demo easy and the production system hard, and most of the work sits in the gap between those two. Some of what is built here reaches people at sensitive moments, where a confidently wrong answer is a harm rather than a bug report; that responsibility is taken seriously and is expected to be shared.
 



 The role also carries a cross\\-cutting mandate. Delivery at Synterra is organised into small, senior pods supported by a central technical group that owns standards, reusable assets, and hard cross\\-project problems. The agent layer built in this seat, together with its evaluation, cost, and safety practices, is expected to become reusable infrastructure that other pods and products build on, not a one\\-off implementation.
 



  





**Key responsibilities** 




 •    
 **Multi\\-agent architecture:** 
 selecting the right topology per problem (supervisor and worker, hierarchical delegation, parallel fan\\-out with a reducer, router, critique and repair loops), including the judgment to use a plain deterministic workflow when an agent adds nothing. A documented rationale is expected for each choice, so decisions remain reviewable as the system grows.
 



 •    
 **Interop layer:** 
 building and operating MCP servers that expose platform capabilities as tools, and applying A2A or comparable protocols where agents discover and delegate to each other across service boundaries.
 



 •    
 **Production Python services:** 
 async REST and streaming endpoints, long\\-running and background execution, durable state and checkpointing, resumability, idempotent tools, retries, and clean API contracts for the platform services that consume the agent layer.
 



 •    
 **Context engineering as a discipline:** 
 context budgeting, compaction and summarisation, sub\\-agent context isolation, scratchpads, and short\\- and long\\-term memory designed so earlier turns do not quietly poison later ones.
 



 •    
 **Caching strategy end to end:** 
 prompt and context caching, cache\\-friendly prefix design so hit rates are genuinely high, TTL and invalidation, and semantic and response caching where appropriate.
 



 •    
 **Dynamic model selection:** 
 routing by task difficulty, latency budget, and required capability; cascades that start small and escalate only when needed; and evals that demonstrate the cheap path is good enough before it is relied upon.
 



 •    
 **Token and cost observability:** 
 span\\-level tracing with token and cost attribution per run, per feature, and per tenant; budgets and hard ceilings; and alerts when a change regresses cost rather than quality.
 



 •    
 **Portability:** 
 an abstraction layer over providers that absorbs differences in tool calling, structured output, caching semantics, and rate limits, so that switching vendor is a week’s work rather than a rewrite.
 



 •    
 **Retrieval quality:** 
 chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, grounding, correct citations, and systems that say “I don’t know” when they should.
 



 •    
 **Evaluation infrastructure:** 
 trajectory and tool\\-call evals, golden sets, regression suites, calibrated LLM\\-as\\-judge, human review, and online metrics. Nothing ships on intuition alone.
 



 •    
 **Guardrails and failure behaviour:** 
 input and output filtering, refusal behaviour, prompt\\-injection resistance for any agent exposed to untrusted content or tool results, sandboxed and least\\-privilege tool execution, loop and step ceilings, fallback across providers when one degrades, and clean handoff to a human when a conversation calls for one.
 



 •    
 **Reusable assets and standards:** 
 evaluation practices, cost playbooks, and reference architectures from this layer documented and packaged so other pods can adopt them; internal guidance provided when other teams integrate agent capabilities into client work.
 



  





**Required skills and experience** 




 •    
 **Production track record:** 
 agent or LLM systems shipped to production users and lived with through the evals, incidents, cost surprises, and quality complaints that follow.
 



 •    
 **Strong coding ability:** 
 solid Python across async and concurrency, typing, testing, packaging, and profiling, with the ability to read a framework’s source when its abstraction gets in the way. Framework glue is not sufficient.
 



 •    
 **Python web services owned in production:** 
 async request handling, streaming responses, background workers, deployment, and on\\-call, not an endpoint wrapped around a notebook.
 



 •    
 **Graph or state\\-machine orchestration depth:** 
 explicit state, checkpointing and durable execution, human\\-in\\-the\\-loop steps, and recovery when a step fails midway, in whichever library the work was done.
 



 •    
 **Multi\\-agent design experience:** 
 the ability to argue clearly about topology, state ownership, delegation, failure isolation, and where a given pattern breaks down.
 



 •    
 **Hands\\-on MCP experience:** 
 ideally having written a server rather than only consumed one, with familiarity with A2A or comparable interop approaches.
 



 •    
 **Practical caching depth:** 
 what actually gets cached, why hit rates collapse, and how to structure prompts so they do not.
 



 •    
 **Inference cost and latency management:** 
 model routing and tiering, cascades, batch inference, streaming and time\\-to\\-first\\-token, and honest measurement of the trade\\-off against quality.
 



 •    
 **Measurement first:** 
 tracing, token accounting, and cost attribution that can be pointed at rather than estimated. Instrumentation precedes optimisation.
 



 •    
 **Structured output reliability:** 
 tool and function calling, structured output, and reliable schema\\-conformant results from a probabilistic system.
 



 •    
 **Empirical method:** 
 prompt and context engineering treated as an empirical discipline, measured, versioned, and tested, with evaluation built before the feature, and a precise account of how improvement is known rather than assumed.
 



 •    
 **Cloud experience:** 
 managed inference, queues, storage, and batch compute, with a working grasp of what each run actually costs.
 



 •    
 **Care with user data:** 
 minimising what reaches a model, respecting regional data\\-residency constraints, and treating logging and training decisions as deliberate choices, never defaults.
 



 •    
 **Honest system assessment:** 
 clear\\-eyed about what these systems cannot do, and willing to say so before a feature is built on a false assumption.
 



 •    
 **Independent execution:** 
 the ability to take an ambiguous product idea, decide whether an agent is even the right answer, and deliver without close supervision.
 



  





**Good to have** 




 •    Breadth across model providers and hosted inference platforms, with a view on where each is genuinely stronger.
 



 •    Breadth across agent orchestration frameworks and vendor agent SDKs, including judgment on when to drop the framework and orchestrate directly.
 



 •    Tracing and eval tooling such as LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize, or OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.
 



 •    Constrained decoding, or serving and tuning open\\-weight models, including distillation to build a cheap tier for a routing cascade.
 



 •    Classical ML and NLP, so a classifier is reached for when a classifier is the right answer, including for routing and difficulty prediction.
 



 •    A second language alongside Python, sufficient to work across the boundary into the platform’s other services.
 



 •    Recommendation, matching, or ranking systems, and the fairness and explainability questions they raise.
 



 •    Multilingual and low\\-resource language work, especially Indian languages; speech synthesis or recognition.
 



 •    AI\\-assisted development in daily practice, with every line shipped remaining fully explainable and debuggable.
 



  





**What the role offers** 




 Competitive salary based on experience, real authority over how the agent layer is architected, influence over company\\-wide AI engineering standards, and features that go from idea to user\\-facing in weeks.
 



  





**How to apply** 




 Please send a resume to
 **careers@synterrait.com** 
 along with anything built: repos, demos, evals, write\\-ups. Applications should briefly describe one agent system shipped to production: how it was structured, how success was measured, and what it cost to run. One system explained deeply is weighted far more heavily than a long list of tools.

**About the role** 




 Delivery is organised into small, senior pods who own a client outcome end to end: scope, architecture, delivery, quality, and production. AI coding agents are an integral part of the delivery workflow, and much of the implementation is agent\\-generated. The value of this role lies in the work that surrounds generation: decomposing ambiguous business problems into buildable specifications, making architectural decisions, directing agents against those decisions, and ensuring that everything shipped meets production standards.
 



 This position owns the web client of a multi\\-product consumer platform shipped across several regions: rendering and caching strategy, Core Web Vitals, the component and design\\-system layer, SEO, localisation, and front\\-end security. The role is problem\\-driven rather than ticket\\-driven. Most engagements are delivered on fixed\\-timeline terms, so scoping and estimation quality has a direct bearing on project outcomes. The emphasis throughout is on engineering judgment.
 



**AI\\-augmented delivery: expectations** 




 •    AI coding agents are used daily as a core part of delivery. The critical skills are the specification that goes into generation and the review that follows it.
 



 •    Full ownership is expected for all code shipped under this role, regardless of how it was produced. Accountability for correctness, security, and maintainability rests with the engineer, not the tool.
 



 •    A key competency is identifying code that appears correct but is not: output that compiles, passes the happy path, and yet conflicts with framework fundamentals, introduces security exposure, or degrades at scale.
 



 •    All AI\\-assisted work is expected to be fully explainable and debuggable by the engineer who ships it.
 



**Key responsibilities** 




 •    
 **Outcome ownership:** 
 scoping, architecture, agent\\-directed implementation, review, testing, and release for web features, delivered end to end.
 



 •    
 **Rendering and caching strategy:** 
 per\\-route selection between static, incremental, server\\-rendered, and client\\-rendered approaches, with a clear understanding of the cost of each. Performance budgets (Core Web Vitals, bundle size, TTFB) are defined, defended, and verified through profiling.
 



 •    
 **Component architecture and design system:** 
 features are built from shared primitives rather than one\\-off markup, so that generated code lands within a coherent system.
 



 •    
 **SEO, metadata, and localisation:** 
 crawlability, structured data, canonical URLs, sitemaps, and multi\\-region routing maintained without forking the codebase.
 



 •    
 **Front\\-end security posture:** 
 CSP, XSS and CSRF defences, safe session and token handling, secrets kept server\\-side, and closure of VAPT findings. Generated code is treated as an additional review surface for security.
 



 •    
 **API boundary:** 
 shaping the contract with the back end, flagging API designs that would force poor rendering choices, and handling auth, real\\-time updates, error and empty states, and optimistic UI to a production standard.
 



 •    
 **Review, mentoring, and standards:** 
 pull requests and agent output reviewed with the same rigour; mentoring of junior engineers within the pod; conventions and reference patterns documented for wider team use.
 



 •    
 **Scoping and estimation:** 
 estimates prepared with care and stood behind, given the direct relationship between scope quality and commercial outcomes on fixed\\-price work.
 



**Required skills and experience** 




 •    
 **Framework depth:** 
 deep production Next.js and React experience on applications shipped and maintained over time. App Router, server components, streaming and suspense, static and incremental generation, server actions, and route handlers.
 



 •    
 **Understanding beneath the API surface:** 
 hydration, the client\\-server boundary, unintended client\\-component conversion, and debugging stale pages across framework cache layers, CDN, and HTTP headers. Review quality at this level is what distinguishes the role.
 



 •    
 **Strong TypeScript:** 
 the type system used to prevent bugs rather than to satisfy the compiler.
 



 •    
 **Breadth of fundamentals:** 
 HTTP, state, data modelling, concurrency, and security fundamentals strong enough to review work at the API and data layer the client consumes. Pods are small, and review responsibility extends across adjacent layers.
 



 •    
 **Performance engineering:** 
 Core Web Vitals, code splitting, bundle analysis, image and font optimisation, and reduction of unnecessary JavaScript.
 



 •    
 **State and data management:** 
 deliberate separation of server and client state, caching and invalidation, and forms and validation, with clear reasoning behind each choice.
 



 •    
 **Accessibility and internationalisation:** 
 semantic markup, keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA where genuinely needed, and internationalised layouts that hold up across languages.
 



 •    
 **Testing:** 
 component and end\\-to\\-end tests as part of normal delivery, with clear judgment on what is worth testing.
 



 •    
 **Independent execution:** 
 the ability to take an ambiguous requirement, clarify what is actually needed, document it clearly enough for others (or agents) to execute, and deliver without close supervision.
 



**Good to have** 




 •    Deploying and operating Next.js outside a managed host: containers, self\\-hosted builds, and an understanding of what the platform layer provides.
 



 •    CI/CD for front end: preview deployments, automated checks, staged rollouts, and feature flags.
 



 •    Front\\-end observability: real user monitoring, error tracking, and session replay.
 



 •    Data privacy in practice: consent management that genuinely gates what it claims to, auditing of third\\-party scripts, PII kept out of URLs, analytics, and logs; familiarity with GDPR and India’s DPDP Act.
 



 •    Monorepo tooling and shared packages across web and other clients.
 



 •    Design\\-system or component\\-library ownership, including documentation and versioning.
 



 •    Analytics, experimentation, and A/B testing infrastructure.
 



**What the role offers** 




 Competitive salary based on experience, direct ownership of technical decisions on the web client, fast delivery cycles supported by AI\\-augmented workflows, and a small senior team environment where engineering judgment is the primary contribution.
